usamo-usamo-1981-01.prompt: Prove that if $n$ is not a multiple of $3$, then the angle $\frac{\pi}{n}$ can be trisected with ruler and compasses.
usamo-usamo-1981-01.answer: Since $\gcd(3,n)=1$, write $1 = 3u + nv$; then $\frac{\pi}{3n} = u\cdot\frac{\pi}{n} + v\cdot\frac{\pi}{3}$, a combination of constructible angles.

usamo-usamo-1981-02.prompt: What is the largest number of towns that can meet the following criteria? Each pair is directly linked by just one of air, bus or train. At least one pair is linked by air, at least one pair by bus and at least one pair by train. No town has an air link, a bus link and a train link. No three towns $A, B, C$ are such that the links between $AB$, $AC$ and $BC$ are all air, all bus or all train.

usamo-usamo-1981-03.prompt: Show that for any triangle, $\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\ge \sin 3A + \sin 3B + \sin 3C \ge -2$. When does the equality hold?
usamo-usamo-1981-03.answer: Upper bound: $\sin3A+\sin3B+\sin(3A+3B)\le 2\sin t(1+\cos t)\le\frac{3\sqrt3}2$; equality iff the angles are $20^\circ,20^\circ,140^\circ$. Lower bound: the smallest of $3A,3B,3C$ is $\le 180^\circ$; $-2$ is approached only in the degenerate limit $A\to0$, $B,C\to 90^\circ$ (never attained by a genuine triangle).

usamo-usamo-1981-04.prompt:
The sum of the measures of all the face angles of a given complete convex polyhedral angle is equal to the sum of the measures of all of its dihedral angles. Prove that the polyhedral angle is a trihedral angle.

(A convex polyhedral angle may be formed by drawing rays from an exterior point $P$ to all points of a convex polygon $A_1A_2\cdots A_n$; its face angles are the angles $\angle A_iPA_{i+1}$ and its dihedral angles are the angles between consecutive planes $PA_{i-1}A_i$ and $PA_iA_{i+1}$. "Trihedral" means $n=3$.)
usamo-usamo-1981-04.answer: On the unit sphere around $P$ the polyhedral angle cuts out a convex spherical $n$-gon with side lengths = face angles and angles = dihedral angles. Its area gives $\sum(\text{dihedral}) > (n-2)\pi$, while $\sum(\text{face angles}) < 2\pi$; so $(n-2)\pi<2\pi$ and $n=3$.
usamo-usamo-1981-04.reviewNote: The AoPS wiki statement (a Kalva paraphrase) compares the dihedral angles with the angles of the polygon; under that reading the hypothesis is impossible for every n (the dihedral angles always sum to more than (n-2)π). The prompt uses the original USAMO wording (face angles at P); please confirm against an official source.

usamo-usamo-1981-05.prompt:
Show that for any positive real $x$ and any positive integer $n$,
$$[nx]\ge \sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{[kx]}{k},$$
where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer not exceeding $x$.
usamo-usamo-1981-05.answer: With $a_k=\{kx\}$ the claim is $\sum_{k\le n} a_k/k\ge a_n$; since $a_{k+m}\le a_k+a_m$, prove it by strong induction, splitting off the last $m$ terms where $m$ minimizes $a_m/m$.
